nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: Edmund. I heard about Clara. Terrible business.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: You look like you haven't slept in days. Are you alright?

nodes.speaker: Edmund
nodes.text: You've been covering the Ripper killings for two years. Every detail. The wounds. The patterns.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: Yes, I've covered them. That's my job.

nodes.speaker: Edmund
nodes.text: Someone staged Clara's death to look like a Ripper killing. Whoever did it knew things that weren't in print.

choices.text: Where were you on the night of the fourteenth?
I saw you near Whitmore Street two weeks ago. What were you doing there?
[Slam his notes onto the desk.] You know exactly what I'm suggesting.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: I was at the Anchor with four other journalists until one in the morning. You can verify it yourself.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: I was following the Hargrove housing story. Different angle to your wife, but the same story. Edmund — Hargrove has connections everywhere. You need to be careful.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: I didn't kill Clara. Edmund, I liked her. She was a better journalist than either of us and she didn't even have the job.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: The unpublished detail you're thinking of — the specific wound pattern — I submitted it to Crane for the January edition. He killed that paragraph too.

nodes.speaker: Silas Webb
nodes.text: Someone with access to our unpublished copy could have had that detail. Not me, Edmund. Someone else.
nodes.journal_entry: Crane killed Webb's paragraph about the Ripper wound pattern. The copycat would have needed exactly that detail. Who sees copy before it prints? Arthur. Only Arthur.
